convert_room_crud_to_shallow_routed_moda.s:
Current state: room *creation* is already a modal (rooms/+page.svelte:198-216, ``), but room *editing* is an inline toggled form, not a modal (src/routes/app/rooms/[id]/+page.svelte:354-370, `{#if editing}
...
{/if}` toggled by the "edit" button at line 311). Neither uses SvelteKit shallow routing — confirmed zero `pushState`/`replaceState` usage from `$app/navigation` anywhere in the repo (only an unrelated local variable also named `pushState` in profile.ts for push-notification permission state — do not confuse the two, that one is untouched by this step). This is net-new wiring, no existing pattern to copy. Part 1 — convert the room-edit inline form into a `Modal`, mirroring the already-correct create-room modal's shape. In src/routes/app/rooms/[id]/+page.svelte, replace the `{#if editing}...{/if}` block (lines 354-370) with: ```svelte
(e.preventDefault(), save_edits())}>
``` `editing` (already `$state(false)`, line 45) becomes the modal's own `bind:open` — no new variable needed, the existing toggle button (line 311, `onclick={() => (editing = !editing)}`) keeps working unchanged since `Modal.svelte`'s `open` prop is bindable. Add `etags = $state(g.tags ?? [])`, `etagInput = $state('')`, `eroom_state = $state<'a'|'p'|'c'>(g.roomState ?? 'a')` alongside the existing `ename`/`edesc`/`ecountry` state (lines 46-50), with `addTag`/`removeTag` functions identical in shape to [[add_room_tags_field]]'s create-modal versions. Update `save_edits()` (lines 192-208) to include `tags: etags, room_state: eroom_state` in the PATCH body. Part 2 — wire both modals (create on rooms/+page.svelte, edit on rooms/[id]/+page.svelte) to SvelteKit shallow routing, so opening either updates the URL (shareable/back-button-able) without a full navigation. Per SvelteKit's shallow-routing API (`pushState`/`replaceState` from `$app/navigation`, associating arbitrary state with a history entry): in rooms/+page.svelte, replace the `creatingOpen` boolean toggle with a shallow-routed equivalent. Add `import { pushState } from '$app/navigation';` and `import { page } from '$app/stores';` (page likely already needed elsewhere — check imports first, add if absent). Replace: ```js let creatingOpen = $state(false); ``` usage with a derived binding off page state, and change the "start a room" button's handler (line 193) from `onclick={() => (creatingOpen = true)}` to: ```js onclick={() => pushState('', { modal: 'create-room' })} ``` and the modal's `bind:open` (line 198) from `bind:open={creatingOpen}` to an open/close pair that reads `$page.state.modal === 'create-room'` and closes via `history.back()`: ```svelte history.back()} title="start a room" > ``` This requires `Modal.svelte` to accept an `onclose` callback distinct from its current pure `bind:open` two-way binding (read Modal.svelte's current props first — it was reported as `bind:open` bindable with its own internal close-button/backdrop-click handling that presumably just flips the bound `open` value; when driven by page state instead of a local `$state`, the modal's internal close paths must call `onclose` rather than directly setting an unbindable derived `open`). Add an optional `onclose?: () => void` prop to Modal.svelte, and in its internal backdrop-click/X-button/Escape handlers, call `onclose?.()` in addition to (or instead of, if `open` is now a plain non-bindable prop when `onclose` is supplied) setting the bound value — the minimal change is: keep `open` bindable as today for every other caller (filters modal, about-room modal, etc. — do not change their call sites), and only in the two call sites touched by this step, pass both `open` and `onclose`, with Modal calling `onclose?.()` from the same internal function that currently flips `open = false`, right before or alongside that flip, so both binding styles keep working. Apply the identical `pushState('', { modal: 'edit-room' })` / `$page.state.modal === 'edit-room'` treatment to the edit-room modal in rooms/[id]/+page.svelte, replacing the `editing` boolean's role as the modal's open-driver (the "edit" button's `onclick={() => (editing = !editing)}` becomes `onclick={() => pushState('', { modal: 'edit-room' })}`; `save_edits()`'s `editing = false` on success becomes `history.back()`). Why shallow routing here specifically (ladder check — is this net-new complexity justified): explicitly requested; the practical payoff is the browser back button closing a modal instead of leaving the room page, and a modal state that survives being an actual navigable/shareable URL fragment (`?` state isn't URL-visible with `pushState`'s state-only form, which is the minimal version — SvelteKit shallow routing also supports state without changing the URL string at all, which is what's used here since these modals don't need their own bookmarkable URL, only history-entry/back-button behavior). Test: extend src/routes/app/rooms/__tests__/page.svelte.test.ts and create src/routes/app/rooms/[id]/__tests__/page.svelte.test.ts (check if the latter directory/file already exists first) with: ```ts it('opens the create-room modal via pushState, not a local flag', async () => { const pushStateMock = vi.fn(); vi.mock('$app/navigation', () => ({ pushState: pushStateMock, goto: vi.fn() })); // render, click "start a room", assert pushStateMock called with { modal: 'create-room' } }); it('closing the modal calls history.back()', async () => { ... }); ``` following the existing render+fireEvent style from MuteButton.svelte.test.ts. Watch fail first, implement, then green. Also manually verify (can't start the dev server per repo rule — note this limitation explicitly rather than skipping verification silently) that `pnpm check` passes for Modal.svelte's new optional prop and both room pages. Run `pnpm test`.

rewrite_site_copy.s:
Full inventory of current user-facing strings to replace, with exact locations: 1. Home page (src/routes/+page.svelte, rebuilt in [[rebuild_home_as_room_search]] — this step supplies the FINAL copy for that page's markup, superseding the provisional text written there): - eyebrow: was `"x2 — meet people through what you're into"` → `"x2 — the room finds you"` - H1: was `find your people.` → `find a room. then your people.` (keeps the italic-accent pattern already established, ``) - subhead: was `"search by vibe. join a room built around what you love. or let us match you with someone new — closest interests first. no feed to scroll, no profile to perform for."` → `"every room here is built around one thing people actually care about. search it, join it, and you're already talking to people who get it — no cold-opens, no empty feed, no profile to perform for first."` - primary CTA: was `"find my people"` (→ `/login`) → `"start free — join or create a room"` (already applied structurally in [[rebuild_home_as_room_search]]'s markup; this step confirms it as final) - search placeholder: `"search rooms by what they're about…"` (unchanged — already good, matches rooms/+page.svelte's existing identical placeholder verbatim, keep them identical across both pages) 2. Nav labels (src/routes/+layout.svelte:39-44, order already changed in [[reorder_nav_rooms_first]]) — labels themselves stay lowercase single words per repo convention (all UI text lowercase): keep `rooms`, `chats`, `profile` as-is; rename `people` → `match` (the page at `/app` is a person-to-person matching/discovery feature, secondary now — "match" telegraphs it's a different, smaller feature rather than implying it's still equally primary; update the `nav` array's third entry label only: `{ href: '/app', label: 'match', icon: Users }`). 3. rooms/+page.svelte (src/routes/app/rooms/+page.svelte): - eyebrow (line 97): was `"rooms — many people, one thread"` → `"your rooms"` (this page is now reached as the primary landing surface, not a secondary nav destination — the eyebrow should orient a just-logged-in user, not re-explain the room concept they already bought into on the home page) - H2 (lines 98-100): was `find a room.
or start one.` → keep verbatim, it already reads well and matches the new primary-surface framing without needing "or" framed as an afterthought — no change. - "joined rooms" eyebrow (line 219): was `"joined rooms"` → `"yours"` (shorter, matches the terser "your rooms" framing above it — avoid saying "room" three times on one screen) - empty state (line 253): was `"you haven't joined a room yet."` → `"nothing yet — search above, or start your own."` (turns a dead-end statement into a next action, standard activation-copy move for an empty state that's now a new user's very first screen) - nothing-matched empty state (line 188): was `"nothing matched. start the room yourself."` → keep verbatim, already does this correctly. 4. app/+page.svelte (the demoted people-matching page, src/routes/app/+page.svelte — read its current copy before editing; not yet audited in prior research, so read the file first to find its exact current headline/CTA strings before writing replacements) — soften from a primary-feature tone to a secondary "also try this" tone consistent with rooms now being primary. Do not remove functionality, only re-tone the copy: if its current headline reads as a primary pitch (e.g. "find your people" repeated), change it to something like `"or skip the room — match one-to-one"` / `"prefer a person over a room? match here."`, framed as an alternative to what the user already did (found rooms), not as the main event. 5. `` title/meta: none exist today anywhere (`src/app.html` has no ``, only `apple-mobile-web-app-title` = "x2"). Add one to the home page for SEO/link-preview purposes, since it's now the primary logged-out landing and public search surface — add to src/routes/+page.svelte's top (before the first `<section>`): ```svelte <svelte:head> <title>x2 — find a room, find your people ``` Marketing-psychology rationale for the specific changes above (brief, since AGENTS.md forbids essay-length unrequested prose but this was explicitly requested — keep to bullet-level): "the room finds you" reframes search as effortless (reduces perceived friction, a known conversion lever over "search for X"); leading with "room" then "people" in the H1 makes the product's actual primary action (joining a room) the first verb a visitor commits to, rather than a vaguer social promise; the empty-state rewrite is a standard "always give the next action" pattern (never leave a user at a dead end); "match" over "people" for the demoted nav label sets correct expectations (a feature, not the whole product) without needing to explain why it moved. Test: this step is copy-only, no new logic — extend whichever component tests already assert on rendered text (src/routes/__tests__/page.svelte.test.ts from [[rebuild_home_as_room_search]], the rooms page test, the layout test) with one assertion per changed string, e.g. `expect(screen.getByText('your rooms')).toBeInTheDocument();` for each of the ~8 changed strings above, so a future accidental copy revert is caught. Watch each new assertion fail against the pre-change text first (temporarily, by running against the old copy mentally/via git stash if easier — or simply confirm the assertion targets text that does not yet exist before implementing), then apply the copy changes, then green. Run `pnpm test`.
